text:
maria: Heads up — canary ramp from 2->3 variants is showing a p95 latency bump ~15% on the gpt-medium mix. Looks correlated with increased fallback events and smaller effective batch sizes.
aj: Do you have a profile or flamegraph?
maria: Quick samples from perf-bot attached below. This was from the 10% canary window at 18:12 UTC. Not huge, but consistent across hosts.
perf-bot: snapshot:
```
perf_summary:
  request_count: 12.8k
  p50_latency_ms: 42
  p95_latency_ms: 178  # baseline p95 ~155
  fallback_rate: 13.8%  # up from 2.1%
kernel_select_time_pct: 21.4%
kv_cache_miss_rate: 37.9%
batch_size_median: 3
batch_size_p95: 10  # baseline p95: 20
socket_queue_depth: increased by 18%
```
linh: kv cache miss up to 38% is concerning. If compat sets are splitting batches, we lose large continuous batches and KV reuse.
aj: Agreed. My suspicion: when routing tries fallback to variant B, we break coalesced windows because compat sets are treated strictly. Result: many small single-request batches hitting different kernels -> extra kernel selection overhead.
ryan: Can we test a "soft compatibility" window where we allow cross-compat batching for up to N ms to favor batch formation, but still prefer strict compat at end of window?
maria: Exactly what I was thinking. Also prefetch KV on fallback could help (warm up cache entries for a variant before kernel run).
aj: Proposed quick config patch for canary:
```
queue_policy:
  name: continuous
  soft_compat_window_ms: 12
  token_budget_per_compat: 640
  prefetch_on_fallback: true
  max_merge_fragmentation: 0.2
```
linh: token_budget bump to 640 aligns with our median token lengths and should allow larger merged batches. soft_compat_window_ms=12 gives room for an extra request or two without hurting latency much.
ryan: One more angle: kernel selection cache currently keyed by (model, variant, seq_len_bucket). With cross-compat batches we should consider relaxing the variant dimension for kernel selection lookup when soft window is active to avoid recompile/mismatch thrash. That needs runtime guard.
aj: Runtime guard: only relax when batch_size >= 4 and combined compat_score >= 0.85. Quick patch exists in my branch aj/soft-compat-kernel-lookup.
perf-bot: Suggest running two canaries in parallel: A) soft_compat_window_ms=6 + prefetch_on_fallback=false, B) soft_compat_window_ms=12 + prefetch_on_fallback=true. Compare p95, kv_miss, and fallback_rate after 30m.
maria: Sounds good. Who wants to own the experiments and metrics query?
ryan: I can wire the dashboards and the ELK queries. I'll add a panel for kernel_select_time_pct and kv_cache_miss_rate by compat_set.
linh: I will prepare the prefetch lambda. It will issue a warmup request for the target variant's recent KV keys on fallback before launching the slower kernel. Simple TTL-backed dedupe.
aj: I'll push the queue policy change and the kernel-lookup guard. Pushing to canary branch now.
infra-bot: deploy started for env=canary, change=aj/soft-compat-kernel-lookup + queue-policy patch.
perf-bot: experiment created: exp_id=exp_2026_03_18_softwin_01. Data window: 18:40-19:10 UTC.
maria: Great — please post the final numbers. If p95 and kv miss improve without raising tail error rates we'll roll to stage. :eyes:
ryan: Quick note — add histogram of batch formation latency (time from first request in batch to dispatched) so we can confirm soft window doesn't add too much queuing.
linh: yep adding metric: batch_wait_ms{compat_window=true}.
aj: rolled out patch to 10% canary group A and B. link: https://dash.redwood/exp/exp_2026_03_18_softwin_01
perf-bot: ack — monitoring.
maria: Thanks team. Follow-up in ~40m with numbers.
